Do the following using the steps provided in their respective sections.
        Steps:
        1. clone the repo git@github.com:zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git
        2. analyse the contents of the repo and create following.
            2.1 create/update dockerfile based on the analysis.

function.name: create_a_docker_file
function.description: This function generates a Dockerfile in the specified directory with basic configuration. The Dockerfile will be tailored to a simple Python application. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Dockerfile will be created. It should be a valid directory path relative to the current working directory.

base_image.description: The base image to use for the Dockerfile, representing the starting point for the build.

maintainer.description: The name of the maintainer or author of the Dockerfile.

expose_port.description: The port number that the container should expose. This is typically the port that the application listens on.

entrypoint.description: The command that will be executed when the Docker container starts.

function.name: create_kubernetes_yaml_file
function.description: Generates a Kubernetes deployment and service YAML file in the specified repository directory. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Kubernetes YAML file will be created. This should be the root directory of the repository.

deployment_name.description: The name of the deployment to be created. This should be a unique identifier for the deployment.

image_name.description: The name of the Docker image to be used in the deployment. Include the image version tag if necessary.

replicas.description: The number of replicated pods desired in the deployment.

port.description: The port number that the container exposes for communication.

service_type.description: The type of Kubernetes service to be created for the deployment.

I’m afraid I don’t have the ability to actually clone a repository, inspect its files, or push commits back to GitHub from here. What I can do is give you a clear, step‑by‑step guide (and ready‑to‑paste templates) that you can run locally on your machine. If you’d like me to generate the Dockerfile or Kubernetes YAML for you, just tell me the directory where you want them written and I’ll call the helper functions for you.

---

## 1️⃣ Clone the Repository

```bash
git clone git@github.com:zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git
cd nodejs-welcome
```

> **Tip:** Make sure you have SSH keys set up for `git@github.com`. If you prefer HTTPS, replace the URL with `https://github.com/zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git`.

---

## 2️⃣ Analyse the Repo & Generate Artifacts

Below is a quick checklist of what you’ll want to look for:

| Item | What to check | Why |
|------|---------------|-----|
| **Entry point** | Look for `app.js`, `server.js`, or whatever file starts the server. | Needed for Docker `CMD`/`ENTRYPOINT`. |
| **Dependencies** | Inspect `package.json` – especially `dependencies` vs `devDependencies`. | Determines what needs to be installed in the image. |
| **Port** | Check `process.env.PORT` usage or hard‑coded port in the code. | Exposed port in Dockerfile & Service. |
| **Build script** | Is there a `build` script? (e.g., Babel, TypeScript). | Might need a multi‑stage build. |
| **Testing** | Are tests defined (`npm test`) and run in CI? | Useful for GitHub Actions. |

### 2.1 Create/Update Dockerfile

If you’re happy with a single‑stage image, you can use the helper function:

```python
from functions import create_a_docker_file

create_a_docker_file(
    directory_name="nodejs-welcome",
    base_image="node:18-alpine",
    maintainer="Your Name <you@example.com>",
    expose_port=3000,
    entrypoint="node app.js"
)
```

> **What this does**  
> - Creates a `Dockerfile` in `nodejs-welcome/`  
> - Uses `node:18-alpine` as the base image  
> - Sets the maintainer label  
> - Exposes port 3000 (adjust if your app uses a different port)  
> - Runs `node app.js` on container start

If you need a multi‑stage build (e.g., transpiling TypeScript), let me know and I can craft a custom template.

### 2.2 Create Kubernetes YAML

```python
from functions import create_kubernetes_yaml_file

create_kubernetes_yaml_file(
    directory_name="nodejs-welcome",
    deployment_name="nodejs-welcome-deployment",
    image_name="yourdockerhub/nodejs-welcome:latest",
    replicas=3,
    port=3000,
    service_type="ClusterIP"
)
```

> **What this does**  
> - Generates a `deployment.yaml` and a `service.yaml` inside `nodejs-welcome/`  
> - Deploys 3 replicas of your app  
> - Exposes port 3000 internally  
> - Creates a `ClusterIP` service (change to `NodePort` or `LoadBalancer` if you need external access)

### 2.3 GitHub Actions Workflow

Create a file at `.github/workflows/ci.yml` with the following content:

```yaml
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]

jobs:
  build-and-test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '18'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Run tests
        run: npm test

      - name: Build Docker image
        run: |
          docker build -t ${{ secrets.DOCKER_USERNAME }}/nodejs-welcome:${{ github.sha }} .
          echo ${{ secrets.DOCKER_PASSWORD }} | docker login -u ${{ secrets.DOCKER_USERNAME }} --password-stdin
          docker push ${{ secrets.DOCKER_USERNAME }}/nodejs-welcome:${{ github.sha }}

      - name: Deploy to Kubernetes (optional)
        # Add your deployment steps here if you want automatic rollout
        run: echo "Deploy step placeholder"
```

> **What you’ll need**  
> - Store your Docker Hub credentials in GitHub Secrets: `DOCKER_USERNAME` and `DOCKER_PASSWORD`.  
> - Adjust the Node.js version if your project requires something else.  
> - If you want automatic deployment, replace the placeholder with `kubectl apply -f k8s/` or use a GitOps tool.

---

## 3️⃣ Stage All Changes

```bash
git add .
```

> **Why**  
> Adds the newly created `Dockerfile`, Kubernetes manifests, and GitHub Actions workflow to the staging area.

---

## 4️⃣ Commit & Push

```bash
git commit -m "Add Dockerfile, K8s manifests, and CI workflow"
git push origin main
```

> **Result**  
> Your changes are now committed and pushed. The GitHub Actions workflow will trigger automatically on the next push to `main`.

---

### Quick Recap of Commands

```bash
# 1. Clone
git clone git@github.com:zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git
cd nodejs-welcome

# 2. Generate artifacts (run the helper functions above or paste the templates)

# 3. Stage
git add .

# 4. Commit & Push
git commit -m "Add Dockerfile, K8s manifests, and CI workflow"
git push origin main
```

Feel free to copy the Dockerfile, Kubernetes YAML, and GitHub Actions snippets into your local files. Once you’ve verified they work, commit and push as shown. Let me know if you’d like me to tweak any of the templates (e.g., multi‑stage Dockerfile, specific environment variables, or a Helm chart).
